acceptanceCriteria: Retained measurement of /bin/ps snapshot latency on a loaded macOS host (load average about 60) and a quiet host, with the chosen bound or adaptive rule justified from it in a build-log entry.

With the bound changed, internal/update version-probe tests (including TestUPDV0005 and TestUPDV0009) and the BBF descendant-snapshot paths pass under synthetic CPU contention sized to the CPU count, and a genuinely hung ps still fails closed with the existing unavailable-snapshot outcome within a stated bound.
No caller loses its fail-closed behaviour: an unavailable snapshot is still reported as unavailable, never as an empty descendant set; focused tests, -race, and sealed change evidence are retained.
body: Reported by the V1-1364 lane (PR beamfall/corvint#877) on 2026-10-14 and checked by the orchestrator at origin/main 92c298a6e. internal/procgroup/descendants.go:23 sets descendantSnapshotTimeout = time.Second, and line 87 applies it to the /bin/ps snapshot. Under host load of about 50-60 on darwin, /bin/ps took about 1.5 s. As a result every version-probing test in internal/update failed, including unchanged ones (TestUPDV0009, TestUPDV0005). The live `corvint-update check` also failed on its first attempt for both Core and Tasks and passed on retry. The lane passed its tests only with a temporarily widened timeout, which it did not commit. The V1-1366 lane saw the same class as BBF 'descendant snapshot unavailable' failures. Expected: a loaded but healthy host completes the snapshot. Actual: a fail-closed refusal. Related, but distinct: V1-0568 (explaining an unavailable snapshot in the desktop sandbox) and the V1-0849 load-test umbrella. Host go1.27.2, darwin.
title: procgroup: 1 s descendantSnapshotTimeout fails /bin/ps snapshots on a loaded host (update probes, BBF)
